background_rationale: After Navy service and roles at insurers, an automaker and a consulting firm, he spent 14 years at Prudential running business units, from Workplace Solutions to all U.S. businesses to International and PGIM.

notable.summary: Announced a leadership realignment effective Feb. 2, 2026, under which U.S. Businesses, Emerging Markets, Japan and PGIM report directly to him, saying the aim was "a more agile, more focused Prudential."

After an internal investigation found employee misconduct in investment solicitations, Prudential of Japan began a voluntary 90-day suspension of new sales and set up a customer reimbursement program; Sullivan said rebuilding customer trust was a top priority.
The board named Sullivan Chairman, combining the roles after Executive Chairman Charles Lowrey stepped down.

Reporting second-quarter results, Sullivan said the strategy is to unlock Prudential's asset management, retirement and protection capabilities through deeper integration and greater use of its scale.

personal_story.hook: Andy Sullivan began his career as a nuclear submarine officer and now chairs and runs Prudential Financial.
personal_story.summary: Sullivan graduated from the U.S. Naval Academy in Annapolis and served as a nuclear submarine officer, earning the Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal. He then worked at DaimlerChrysler, Diamond Technology Partners, Cigna and CareFirst BlueCross BlueShield before joining Prudential in 2011. At Prudential he led Workplace Solutions, then all U.S. businesses, then the international insurance operations and PGIM, before becoming CEO in March 2025 and chairman in March 2026.
